Tuolumne River

Sadie Gill, Mark Tompkins

July 2020

Future Data Improvement

None expected.

Instream Spawning and Rearing Habitat

Data Source: Methods for Quantifying Existing and Future Suitable Habitat for Fall-run Chinook Salmon, 2024

Instream spawning and rearing habitat for Fall Run Chinook Salmon in the Tuolumne River were provided by William Sears and Tuolumne parties as part of the Healthy Rivers and Landscapes modeling effort. The TUFlow modeling report from the FERC relicensing, which describes the process for developing the 1D/2D surface from which rasters of depth and velocity were derived for the entire 50 mile reach of the lower Tuolumne River. These were provided in units of suitable acres.

Steelhead

Steelhead were assigned Fall Run Chinook values.

Spawning and Rearing Data

The instream spawning and rearing habitat data described above for Fall Run Chinook Salmon (FR) were used for Steelhead (ST). Units are in suitable acres and converted to square meters.

Spawning WUA

The following plot shows the spawning suitable area in square meters for Fall Run Chinook Salmon and Steelhead. Steelhead values are assumed to be the same as Fall Run Chinook.

Rearing WUA

The following plot shows the rearing WUA in square feet per thousand feet for Fall Run Chinook Salmon and Steelhead fry and juvenile. These rates are multiplied by the total rearing reach length mapped by the SIT to estimate available habitat.
